newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures still lower AM on origins.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures still lower AM on origins.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures slowed their decline by Monday midsession in brisk trade with July regaining a foothold at above $1,600 after battling with the key support level.
Traders said origin offers hammered the market lower from the opening bell amid pre-opening expectations of $50-$80 down.
But London, as usual, failed to fulfil its due and prices just gapped about $10-$40 down on the nearbys.

Benchmark July was driven to a low of $1,595 a tonne after breaching the closely-watched $1,600 barrier. But roaster and trade buying at the lows managed to push it back to the $1,600 territory in late morning.
By the morning close, it stood $20 down at $1,608, the same as the opening level.
The market was called sharply lower after steep New York losses on Friday after news truck drivers in Colombia agreed to end their six-day strike.
Midday volume in London reached 3,951 lots. Active May/July switches were traded at $35-$48 under with a good volume done at $40.
Traders called New York to open $2.50 higher.
Pending a sharp movement in New York, the London market is likely to stay in a tight range with the upside being capped by origin selling notably from Indonesia.
But the downside risk seemed limited.
"Roasters still have a lot of price-fixing to do," said one trader. "This is likely to keep the market above the $1,550 area." -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
